issues.description: `Farm.singFarmSong()` is specified and stubbed to print the song with signature `public void singFarmSong()`, but the reference solution implements it as `public String singFarmSong()` returning the song text. This API mismatch will cause student implementations to diverge from the expected method contract (printing vs returning) and can break compilation against tests expecting the other signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the contract across problem statement, template, and solution: either (a) change the solution to `public void singFarmSong()` and print verses, or (b) change the problem statement and template to require `public String singFarmSong()` and adjust wording/comments to “returns the song text” (and tests accordingly).

issues.description: `Farm.singFarmSongVerse(Animal)` is defined in the UML as a `private void` helper that prints a verse, but the solution implements it as `private String singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)` returning the verse text. This inconsistency makes it unclear whether the helper should print or return text and is coupled to the `singFarmSong()` return-type change.
issues.suggestedFix: Make `singFarmSongVerse` consistent with the chosen approach: if the assignment expects printing, use `private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)` and print inside; if returning is preferred, update the UML/problem statement (and template stub) to specify `private String singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)`.

issues.description: The template stub declares `singFarmSongVerse` without an `Animal` parameter (parameter is commented out as `/*Animal animal*/`), while the UML/problem statement and solution require a parameterized helper accepting an `Animal`. This leaves students without a clear required signature in the starter code.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template to declare the parameter explicitly: `private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)` (or `private String ...` if adopting the return-text approach), matching the UML/problem statement and reference implementation.
